## The dataset

The hazard data come from the Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS) dataset
[`sis-european-wind-storm-reanalysis`](https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/sis-european-wind-storm-reanalysis),
a catalogue of European windstorms from 1940 to 2026 derived from reanalysis.
Storms are identified by one of two tracking algorithms, Hodges and
TempestExtremes; njord uses the Hodges tracks. A CDS account is needed to
download anything.

The dataset has three products:

- **Summary indicators.** One row per year, NUTS region and gust threshold
  (0, 15.6, 20 and 25 m/s), giving the number of storms and statistics of the
  gusts they brought to the region.
- **Tracks.** The path of each storm: one row per storm per 6-hour time step,
  with the position of the storm centre, the mean sea level pressure and the
  gust there.
- **Footprints.** One gridded field per storm: the maximum 10 m gust at each
  grid cell over a 72-hour window.

## Why the footprints

The hazard model needs a severity for each storm, measured over the UK. Only
the footprints provide one.

The summary indicators look like the natural starting point, since they are
already aggregated to UK regions. But their values are yearly: the storm
severity index (SSI) in a row is for all the storms of that year in that
region, not for any one storm. It is also computed from the mean gust, the
cube of the mean gust scaled by the area affected, so it adds nothing to the
mean gust itself.

The tracks are per storm, but the gust they record is at the storm centre.
That is not where the strongest winds are, and the centre need not be over the
UK at all.

So the per-storm severity is computed from the footprints, and the other two
products play supporting parts. The tracks say which storms exist and when
each one started, which is what the footprint download needs. The summary
indicators give yearly storm counts to check against. <!-- TODO - this needs to be verified! -->

## Tracks first

The footprints cannot be downloaded in one go. The CDS serves them one storm
at a time, and a storm is asked for by the date it started: a year, a month
and a day. So the start dates have to be known first, and they come from the
tracks.

The tracks can be had in a single request for all storms, which is what
[`download_tracks.R`](https://github.com/awkward-crow/njord/blob/main/inst/scripts/download_tracks.R)
does. The result is a zip holding one CSV. Each storm has an id, and its start
date is the date of its earliest time step.

The download of 2026-09-28 has 1,905 storms, starting on 1,826 distinct dates:
on 75 dates more than one storm started.

## Downloading the footprints

<!-- TODO: add something about how numbers that follow refer to a download carried out on 2026-09-28 and check the number of storms etc -->

[`download_footprints.R`](https://github.com/awkward-crow/njord/blob/main/inst/scripts/download_footprints.R)
reads the start dates from the tracks zip and downloads the footprint of every
storm.

A request can list several days, as long as they are in the same month. So the
script groups the start dates by year and month and sends one request for each
year-month that has storms, 721 requests in all. Each request returns a zip
with one NetCDF file per storm, named with the storm's start date and track id.

The footprints are requested at the original 0.25° resolution, covering the
storm's footprint area rather than the full domain.

A download of this size takes hours and is likely to be interrupted. The
script skips any year-month whose zip already exists, so running it again
carries on where it stopped.

## Checking the download

With 721 requests, a missing or damaged file would be easy to overlook.
[`check_footprints.sh`](https://github.com/awkward-crow/njord/blob/main/inst/scripts/check_footprints.sh)
compares what was downloaded with the tracks, without extracting anything. It
checks that:

- every zip is intact;
- every storm in the tracks has a footprint, and only one;
- no footprint belongs to a storm that is not in the tracks;
- the date in each footprint's filename is its storm's start date.

For the download of 2026-09-28 all four hold: 721 zips, 1,905 footprints for
1,905 storms, and no date mismatches.

The scripts' own
[readme](https://github.com/awkward-crow/njord/blob/main/inst/scripts/Readme.md)
has the details of what each one writes and the order to run them in.

## What a footprint contains

Each footprint is a small NetCDF file, 50 to 60 KB, holding a single gridded
variable, `decontaminated_footprint`. Its value at a grid cell is the maximum
10 m gust there over a 72-hour window of the storm.

Every footprint is on the same grid: 0.25° cells from 25°W to 35°E and from
30°N to 70°N, which is 241 cells by 161. Because the grid is fixed, footprints
can be compared or stacked cell by cell without any regridding.

Only the cells near the storm have values. Cells more than 1000 km from the
track are `NaN`, so a footprint says nothing about gusts far from the storm,
and a storm that passed well away from the UK has no UK values at all.

The file does not say which cells are land. A land-sea mask has to come from
somewhere else before gusts over the UK can be picked out.

The filename carries the storm's start date and its track id, and the id is
the same as the `id` in the tracks CSV. That is how a footprint is tied back to
its storm.
